assertions.name: manybody_residual_decouples_from_nucleon_count
assertions.source: the Li many-body residual is roughly constant (8.84, 7.68, 8.13 MeV, CV 5.8% < 10%) while the nucleon 3-clique count grows +43% (>30%) — decoupled ⇒ the many-body term is not a nucleon-level count but the α-cluster structure (GAP-4), so the nucleon graph→link promotion is the wrong level.

description: GAP-2b diagnostic (qou-ooqh→GAP-4 bridge): with e₂,e₃ pinned on D,T and the max-contact 2-body backbone (GAP-1), the many-body residual across ⁵Li/⁶Li/⁷Li is roughly CONSTANT (~8.2 MeV, CV~6%) while the nucleon 3-clique count grows +43% — they DECOUPLE, and the demanded_M₃ (~4.3–4.9) matches no nucleon deltahedral invariant. So a universal-e₃ × nucleon count cannot supply the residual; the near-constant residual is the α-cluster signature (⁵Li=α+p, ⁶Li=α+d, ⁷Li=α+t share a ~constant α-core many-body binding). The many-body term is at the α-cluster level (GAP-4 / #3551 Brink deltahedra), NOT the nucleon-level μ̄-irreducible count — this prunes the nucleon-link-promotion route. Diagnostic (inverts residual, à la Part 6), not a fit; scope-(a); no wiring.
